audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never mentions that Renekton's Fury-empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields on the target.
audit.why: Riot's own ability text for Ruthless Predator reads: at more than 50 Fury he slashes three times, 'destroying damage shields on the target', for high damage and a 1.5s stun instead of 0.75s. Tahm Kench's entire defensive active is a damage shield. Against a full-Fury Renekton, pressing Thick Skin before the W lands does not soften the combo - the shield is deleted and the banked grey health is gone for nothing. This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it is absent from every field.
audit.corrected: Never pre-shield into a full Fury bar: empowered Ruthless Predator destroys the Thick Skin shield outright. Hold E until the W has resolved, or until his Fury is under 50.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells the player to trade 'when his W is on cooldown' but never gives a number, and never mentions Fury as the actual gate.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8 and Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, so at rank 1 both are long. But the thing that decides whether the W is a 0.75s stun or a 1.5s shield-destroying stun is his Fury bar, not the cooldown. A player watching only cooldowns will walk into the empowered version at full health.
audit.corrected: Read the Fury bar first, the cooldown second: under 50 Fury his W is a 0.75s stun you can eat; over 50 it is 1.5s and it eats your shield.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (P Reign of Anger, W, E)

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json carries the autoreset-burst-tell row for this pairing, and the kit flags W as autoReset. The practical consequence is that the wind-up of his auto is the moment to back off - by the time the W animation is visible the damage is already committed.
audit.corrected: His combo opens with an auto into a W reset; the auto wind-up is the tell, not the W cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is never mentioned, even though the full layer's own late-game line says 'anti-heal stays core'.
audit.why: Cull the Meek is a 7-second AoE that heals Renekton off every minion in range, doubled when empowered. That heal is what lets him win the extended trades the entry keeps warning about. Bramble Vest is a natural early buy on a Grasp tank and cuts it.
audit.corrected: Bramble Vest early: Cull the Meek's heal off the wave is what wins him extended trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's W is called 'Abyssal Voyage' in spikes[1], mid, late and whys[4], and is described as arriving at level 6 and as making you 'a global threat'.
audit.why: The live W is Abyssal Dive: 1000-1200 range, knockup, 21/20/19/18/17, learnable from level 2. It is not global and it is not the level-6 ability - Devour is. Sentences pairing 'Abyssal Voyage' with level 6 are wrong on the name, the timing and the range.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (W), a 1000-1200 range knockup available from level 2. Level 6 gives Devour only.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] pins the swing to 'Abyssal Voyage and Tongue Lash stun online together' at level 6.
audit.why: The Tongue Lash stun is available from level 1 - it only needs three An Acquired Taste stacks - and Abyssal Dive arrives at level 2 or 3. Nothing new lands at 6 except Devour. The real level-6 swing is that Devour turns a landed stun into a full removal.
audit.corrected: Level 6 adds Devour, which converts the 3-stack stun you already had into a removal.

edits.before: Renekton's W stun into fury-empowered Q shred is his peak window — getting caught at 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste before you can land your own stun is a kill.
edits.after: Renekton's W stun into fury-empowered Q shred is his peak window — over 50 Fury that W is 1.5 seconds and destroys your Thick Skin shield outright, so never pre-shield it.

edits.before: Your Abyssal Voyage and Tongue Lash stun online together shift this to a genuine coin-flip — one 3-stack Q into Devour punishes any Renekton all-in.
edits.after: Devour arrives and converts the 3-stack Tongue Lash stun you already had into a full removal — one clean stun into Devour punishes any Renekton all-in.

edits.after: Open with an auto into the W reset at full Fury so the 1.5s stun lands and takes your Thick Skin shield with it

edits.after: His Ruthless Predator W lands before you reach 3 An Acquired Taste stacks in most level-2 trades, and above 50 Fury it stuns for 1.5s and destroys the Thick Skin shield on contact.

edits.before: By level 6 this lane finally opens up. Renekton's damage is losing steam relative to your tankiness, and one 3-stack Tongue Lash stun followed by Devour punishes any overextended W-stun attempt on his part — he is briefly removed from the fight and takes bonus damage while inside. Do not use Abyssal Voyage to escape unless you genuinely need to; save it as a re-engage threat that makes him respect the lane. Play around the 3-stack window: poke with Tongue Lash to stack, back off, repeat — when his W is on cooldown and you have 3 stacks, that is the moment to commit.
edits.after: By level 6 this lane finally opens up. Renekton's damage is losing steam relative to your tankiness, and one 3-stack Tongue Lash stun followed by Devour punishes any overextended W-stun attempt on his part — he is briefly removed from the fight and takes bonus damage while inside. Read his Fury bar before you commit: under 50 his W is a 0.75s stun you can absorb, over 50 it is 1.5s and it deletes your Thick Skin shield. Poke with Tongue Lash to stack, back off, repeat — when his Fury is spent and you have 3 stacks, that is the moment.

edits.before: Past first item Renekton is a shell. His damage does not scale and your Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis lets Thick Skin grey-health healing eat trades he would have won at level 4. The Devour combo is a clean punish in every skirmish — stun him into swallow, deny his damage window, and let your team clean up. Abyssal Voyage makes you a global threat to any teamfight your team needs. Respect nothing from him in a straight fight at this point; the only way you lose the lane post-items is giving away kills during his early power window and spot-feeding him enough gold to survive into mid-game.
edits.after: Past first item Renekton is a shell. His damage does not scale and your Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis lets Thick Skin grey-health healing eat trades he would have won at level 4. The Devour combo is a clean punish in every skirmish — stun him into swallow, deny his damage window, and let your team clean up. Bramble Vest or Thornmail keeps Cull the Meek from healing him back off the wave. Respect nothing from him in a straight fight at this point; the only way you lose the lane post-items is giving away kills during his early window and feeding him enough gold to survive to mid-game.

edits.before: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: matchup-defining — Empowered = long stun. W-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: 16s at rank 1, but read the Fury bar, not the timer. Over 50 Fury it stuns 1.5s and destroys your Thick Skin shield — hold E until it resolves. - Devour: kill windows only.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Renekton's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour turns your 3-stack stun into a removal. Dominus gives him bonus health and free Fury — reassess every all-in at 6.

notes: The full layer's dosFull[1] reads 'W-dodge his empowered W', which is not a real option: Ruthless Predator is a 300-range point-and-click cast, so Abyssal Dive cannot dodge it once it is cast. The honest instruction is to not be at 300 units while his Fury bar is above 50. Left unedited because dosFull is an array of objects and I kept full-layer edits to the granular paths the spec names explicitly.
